content.text: Anchor lookup uses the exact pathname; the path check tolerates trailing-slash differences but the anchor check doesn't. Fix by also trying the trailing-slash variants.

cd /testbed/packages/docusaurus/src/server; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='brokenLinks.ts'
s=open(p).read()
old="""    const targetPage =
      collectedLinks.get(pathname) || collectedLinks.get(decodeURI(pathname));"""
new="""    const targetPage =
      collectedLinks.get(pathname) ||
      collectedLinks.get(decodeURI(pathname)) ||
      // The broken link checker should not care about a trailing slash
      // Those are already covered by the broken pathname checker
      // See https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/issues/10116
      collectedLinks.get(addTrailingSlash(pathname)) ||
      collectedLinks.get(removeTrailingSlash(pathname)) ||
      collectedLinks.get(addTrailingSlash(decodeURI(pathname))) ||
      collectedLinks.get(removeTrailingSlash(decodeURI(pathname)));"""
assert old in s
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new))
EOF
cd /testbed && yarn jest packages/docusaurus/src/server/__tests__/brokenLinks.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -5

content.text:
I fixed this in `packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts`. The 34 existing broken-links tests still pass. I didn't add a test for this exact case and didn't rebuild the reporter's repo.

**Cause:** the checker handles the page path and the anchor separately. The page-path check already accepts a link with or without a trailing slash. The anchor check didn't: it looked up the target page using the link's path exactly as written. An index page like `/docs/php/tooling` is collected as `/docs/php/tooling/`, so `/docs/php/tooling#phpunit` found no page and every anchor on it was reported as broken.

**Fix:** if the exact lookup fails, the anchor check now also tries the path with the trailing slash added and removed (including the URL-decoded version).

This applies to every page, even routes marked as trailing-slash sensitive (`strict`). That's fine because a link to a path that doesn't exist is still caught by the page-path check before anchors are checked.
